diagnostic_evidence.quote: Property (i) is a direct consequence of optimization.
We use 3 epochs for each JKO step
This approach accelerates the particle updates and preserves all physical quantities without significantly impacting the accuracy

issues.failure_explanation: The only argument for entropy decay (Props. prop:added-3 and prop:added-4(i)) is that the optimal u does at least as well as u=0, so the minimal loss is <= 0 and hence sum_i h_i >= 0. This needs an exact global minimizer of the stated problem. The implemented method trains a non-convex neural network with a few epochs of mini-batch SGD, where each batch contains only within-batch pairs, and then updates particles with a random-batch interaction that differs from the training loss. Nothing in the paper shows the final loss is <= 0, so the decay of the discrete entropy is not guaranteed for the algorithm actually run. The paper also gives no stability result beyond this monotonicity argument, so "unconditional stability" is unsupported. The paper itself only says entropy dissipation is maintained "reasonably well" in an experiment.

failure_location.quote: the proposed method enjoys exact entropy dissipation and unconditional stability

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the guarantee conditionally on the trained u attaining objective value <= 0 (the u=0 comparison). Optionally add a check or safeguard to the algorithm (retrain or reduce tau if the loss is positive). Remove or qualify "unconditional stability".
issues.overall_effect: The headline advantages over score-based methods (exact entropy decay, unconditional stability, usable with large time steps) are established only for the idealized exact-minimizer scheme, not for Algorithm 1 with SGD training and random-batch updates.
issues.title: "Exact entropy dissipation and unconditional stability" claimed for a scheme whose guarantee needs an exact global minimizer
issues.why_classification: The formal propositions stay valid under an exact-minimizer hypothesis, but the central advertised guarantee changes from unconditional to conditional on optimization quality, which needs a rewording plus a safeguard or condition.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we verify that the Landau equation is recovered up to first-order accuracy in time, based on the optimality conditions

issues.failure_explanation: Condition (opt_u1) is derived only at the terminal time t=1, using lambda(1)=-2 tau log f(1). The constraint PDE in (djko) transports f from t=0 to t=1 with u(t,.) for every t in [0,1], and u(t) depends on grad lambda(t), which solves the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. The paper never shows u(t) is approximately tau*grad log f(1) for t<1, e.g. via lambda=O(tau) and d_t lambda=O(tau^2). It also does not control the difference between score evaluations at f^n, f(t) and f^{n+1} (an implicit step). The conclusion that f^{n+1} "is indeed the solution ... after one time step tau" is not what follows. At best an O(tau^2) local error would be obtained, with the score evaluated at f^{n+1}. The promised verification of first-order accuracy is therefore not carried out.

failure_location.quote: into the constraint PDE in \eqref{djko} reveals that $f^{n+1} = f(1, \cdot)$ is indeed the solution of the homogeneous Landau equation \eqref{landau_homo} after one time step $\tau$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the Hamilton-Jacobi equation for lambda to show grad lambda(t) = grad lambda(1) + O(tau^2) on [0,1]. Then expand f(1) from the constraint PDE to obtain f^{n+1} = f^n + tau Q(f^{n+1}, f^{n+1}) + O(tau^2), and state the result as a formal consistency statement.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the dynamical JKO scheme is a first-order-in-tau approximation of the Landau equation is not established. The later use of the score-plus-null-space structure for the network ansatz rests on (opt_u1) at t=1 only.
issues.title: First-order consistency argument substitutes a t=1 optimality condition into the whole-time constraint PDE
issues.why_classification: The gap is fillable with a contained formal-expansion argument using the already-derived HJ equation, without changing the scheme or its claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consequently, the total computational cost per epoch is significantly reduced to $\mathcal{O}(N)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm algorithm_opt computes each step from the B^2 pairs (i,j) in one batch C_q, so one step costs O(B^2), not O(BN). An epoch has N/B steps, so the epoch cost is O(BN). If one step cost O(BN), the epoch would cost O(N^2), contradicting the stated O(N). The O(N) per epoch claim holds only for B=O(1), whereas the paper only assumes B<<N, and the experiments use B=640 to 1280. The later claim that the JKO method "scales as O(N)" inherits this unstated fixed-B assumption.

failure_location.quote: Thus the cost of one gradient descent decreases to $\mathcal{O}(BN)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the step cost as O(B^2) and the epoch cost as O(BN). State that this is linear in N for fixed B, and qualify the empirical O(N) scaling accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised complexity reduction from O(N^2) to O(N) is stated with inconsistent intermediate costs. It is linear in N only when the batch size B is held fixed independently of N.
issues.title: Inconsistent cost accounting for the pair mini-batch SGD (per step vs per epoch)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the complexity statements preserves the method and the (fixed-B) linear-scaling conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma sgd_lemma2 gives the coefficient alpha L^2 B/(2N) multiplying sum_q ||theta_k - theta_{q-1}||^2. Inserting Lemma sgd_lemma1's bound alpha^2 N^2/B^2 (...) gives alpha^3 L^2 N/(2B) (...). The proof instead writes alpha L^2/(2N) * alpha^2 N^2/B^2 = alpha^3 L^2 N/(2B^2), dropping the factor B. The correct noise term is therefore (3 sigma^2 alpha^3 L^2 N)/(2B) and the final bound has error floor 6 sigma^2 L^2 alpha^2 N/B. The stated floor N/B^2 is smaller by a factor B. The descent coefficient (alpha^2 L^2 N/B)(3M+2)-1 also differs from the paper's with N/B^2. The theorem as stated is not a consequence of its proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the arithmetic with the factor B kept. State the error floor as 6 sigma^2 L^2 alpha^2 N/B and re-derive the admissible step-size range, which is implied by the stated one.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative bound in thm_opt_conv (noise floor, and the derivation of the step-size restriction) is unsupported as written. The correct bound has a noise term larger by a factor B.
issues.title: Dropped factor B in the proof of the convergence theorem: stated error floor and step-size analysis do not follow
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short recomputation, but the theorem's stated guarantee changes by a factor B, a limited weakening rather than a mere typo.

issues.failure_explanation: Summing the per-q bounds over q=1..m with m=N/B gives sum q = m(m+1)/2 and sum q^2 = m(m+1)(2m+1)/6. The proof uses the continuum values m^2/2 and m^3/3, which are strictly smaller. The correct coefficient of Delta is 3 alpha_k^2 L^2 (m+1)/(2m), which for m=1 equals 3 alpha_k^2 L^2. Under alpha_k <= 1/(L sqrt 3) this is only <= 1, not <= 1/2, so the absorption step Delta <= 2(...) is not justified. The constants in the lemma's conclusion are therefore wrong in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use exact sums (or bound (m+1)/m by 2) and adjust the step-size condition and the constants in the lemma and theorem accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical constants (3M+2, 3 sigma^2) and the step-size condition derived from them are not exactly justified. The theorem's constants need adjusting.
issues.title: Summation constants in Lemma sgd_lemma1 underestimate sum q and sum q^2
issues.why_classification: A routine constant-tracking repair, e.g. a slightly smaller step-size bound, preserves the structure and conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we first randomly select a batch of indices from $[N]$ and then update parameter $\theta$ based on the gradient information within this batch
The final result is obtained by taking the expectation.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof follows the random-reshuffling argument, where an epoch's batches partition all component indices, so the epoch average of component gradients at theta_k equals the full gradient. Here the batches contain only within-batch pairs: the NB pairs in the union of C_q x C_q are a small subset of the N^2 pairs, so (1/(NB)) sum_q sum_{i,j in C_q} grad l_ij(theta_k) is not grad l(theta_k). The last step of Lemma sgd_lemma2 bounds ||grad l(theta_k) - grad l_ij(theta_{q-1})|| by L||theta_k - theta_{q-1}||. That is false, because it needs grad l_ij(theta_k) = grad l(theta_k). The missing term is a partition-dependent discrepancy, of order the variance in (A.3), and is not small. Pathwise, the lemma can fail, since the within-batch average gradient can be anti-aligned with grad l. The theorem's final line says only "taking the expectation", but no expectation over the random partition is ever computed. In particular, the bias and scaling of the within-batch gradient (including diagonal pairs and the factor (B-1)N/(B(N-1))) is never analysed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a lemma on the random partition: compute the expected within-batch gradient relative to grad l, handling the diagonal terms and scaling, and bound its variance. Redo the descent inequality with an explicit bias/variance term, and update the theorem's constants. Alternatively, change the algorithm so batches of pairs cover all N^2 pairs in each epoch.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence guarantee for the tailored within-batch SGD (Algorithm algorithm_opt) is not established by the given argument. The result is proved for a different, partition-covering reshuffling scheme.
issues.title: Descent lemma treats within-batch pair gradients as if they averaged to the full gradient
issues.why_classification: A contained new lemma on the expected within-batch gradient and a modified descent bound should yield a comparable convergence-to-neighborhood result, but this is more than a routine fix.
